newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin upbeat on U.S. economy, but still cautious.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin upbeat on U.S. economy, but still cautious.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin delivered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economic outlook but said that it was not without its risks.

"The current situation is very good. It's terrific," Rivlin told public television's NewsHour with Jim Lehrer program. "We have good growth, we have low unemployment and we have very little inflation.
"We may be in for -- if we're careful -- a good long period of very good growth," she added.
Wall Street seems to agree. The U.S. stock market capped a record-shattering week with further gains on Friday, buoyed by news that producer prices fell in May for the fifth straight month.
Rivlin, however, cautioned against concluding that it meant that inflation was dead. "It (inflation) may be still to come," she said. "You have to look at what's happening to wages."
With unemployment at a near 24-year low, wage growth is picking up, although not "terribly fast," she said.
"We do have to look at this low unemployment and whether it could be giving us inflationary pressure down the road, because the Fed has to anticipate," Rivlin said.
The stock market is something else the Fed needs to keep an eye on, she said. If the market's continued climb spurs consumer spending, that could add to pressure on the economy.
"One of things one should worry about is that people get too exuberant, particularly in the stock market," Rivlin said.

She added that investors had to be "really optimistic" about the outlook for corporate earnings to justify the high prices that they are paying for stocks. But investors also may be encouraged by signs that economic growth may be slowing from its run-away pace of the first quarter, Rivlin said.
